subject: Physical Sciences

topics.name: MECHANICS: Momentum & impulse
subtopics: Momentum p = mv; vector nature and vector diagrams
Newton's second law in momentum form Fnet = Δp/Δt
Change in momentum under a resultant force
Impulse; impulse-momentum theorem FnetΔt = mΔv (1D); safety applications
Conservation of linear momentum; isolated systems, internal and external forces
Collisions of two objects in one dimension; elastic vs inelastic by calculation

topics.name: MECHANICS: Vertical projectile motion
subtopics: Projectiles; equations of motion for position, velocity and displacement
x-t, v-t and a-t graphs: free fall, thrown up, thrown down, bouncing objects
Equations for position and velocity vs time matching the graphs
Read position, displacement, velocity, acceleration off graphs; describe the motion

topics.name: MATTER & MATERIALS: Organic molecules
subtopics: Definitions: organic molecule, functional group, hydrocarbon, homologous series, saturated, unsaturated, structural isomer
Condensed, structural and molecular formulae (max 8 C, one functional group): alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alcohols, haloalkanes, carboxylic acids, aldehydes, ketones, esters
IUPAC naming (max three alkyl substituents; max two functional groups for haloalkanes)
Saturated/unsaturated compounds; chain, positional and functional isomers
Physical properties (boiling/melting point, vapour pressure) vs IMF strength, functional group, chain length, branching
Combustion of alkanes in excess oxygen; alkanes as fuels
Esterification: equation, reaction conditions, IUPAC names of reactants and products

Classify and write equations for addition (alkenes), elimination (dehydrohalogenation, cracking, dehydration of alcohols) and substitution (hydrolysis of haloalkanes, halogenation of alkanes) reactions

sba: Formal practical (Physics, choose one): conservation of linear momentum OR determine the acceleration due to gravity
Formal practical (Chemistry, option): preparation of three esters OR reactions of alkanes and alkenes with Br2

topics.name: MECHANICS: Work, energy, and power
subtopics: Work done on an object; net work; force and free-body diagrams; positive vs negative net work
Work-energy theorem on horizontal, vertical and inclined planes
Conservative and non-conservative forces; conservation of mechanical energy
Wnc = ΔEk + ΔEp problems
Power; Pave = Fvave at constant speed; minimum motor power (e.g. borehole pumping)

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND & LIGHT: Doppler Effect
subtopics: Doppler effect with sound and ultrasound; pitch change; medical applications (blood flow, foetal heartbeat)
fL = (v±vL)/(v±vs)·fs problems with moving source or listener
Red shifts; Doppler evidence for the expanding universe

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Rate and extent of reaction
subtopics: Reaction rate: definition and calculation from data
Factors affecting rate; collision theory explanation
Experimental techniques for measuring rate (interpret tables and graphs)
Positive catalysts; molecular energy distribution graphs (catalyst, temperature, concentration)

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Chemical equilibrium
subtopics: Open and closed systems; reversible reactions; dynamic equilibrium
Factors influencing equilibrium position; Le Chatelier's principle
Interpret equilibrium graphs
Equilibrium constant Kc: expression, calculations, significance of high/low values

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Acids and bases
subtopics: Arrhenius and Lowry-Brønsted definitions
Strong vs weak, concentrated vs dilute acids and bases; conjugate pairs
Neutralisation reactions; titration calculations; indicator choice
Salt hydrolysis and approximate pH
pH scale; pH of strong acids and bases; Kw and auto-ionisation of water
Ka and Kb of strong vs weak acids/bases; comparison by pH, conductivity and reaction rate

sba: Formal practical (Physics): work done and power expended walking/running up a flight of stairs
Formal practical (Chemistry, option): effect of temperature and concentration on Na2S2O3 + HCl reaction rate OR any factor affecting rate
Formal practical (Chemistry): titration — unknown concentration of an acid or base against a standard solution
June examination (two papers, 150 marks, 3 hrs each) OR control test (150 marks: 75 Physics + 75 Chemistry)

topics.name: CONTROL TEST: Discussion, corrections, remedial work
ELECTRICITY & MAGNETISM: Electric circuits
subtopics: Current, voltage, resistance in series/parallel networks (max four resistors)
Internal resistance; ε = IRext + Ir
Circuit problems combining internal resistance with series/parallel arrangements

topics.name: ELECTRICITY & MAGNETISM: Electrodynamics
subtopics: Generators: energy conversion, electromagnetic induction, AC vs DC generators, components
Motors: motor effect, components, uses
Advantages of AC over DC; voltage-time and current-time graphs for AC
rms values: Irms = Imax/√2, Vrms = Vmax/√2; average power (purely resistive circuits)

topics.name: MATTER & MATERIALS: Optical phenomena and properties of materials
subtopics: Photoelectric effect and its significance; threshold frequency f0; work function W0
Photoelectric equation E = W0 + Kmax (E = hf, W0 = hf0, Kmax = ½mv²max)
Effect of intensity and frequency; particle nature of light
Atomic spectra via energy transitions; absorption vs emission spectra

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Electrochemical reactions
subtopics: Oxidation and reduction (electron transfer, oxidation numbers); oxidising/reducing agents; anode, cathode, electrolyte
Galvanic cells: salt bridge, ion movement, electron flow, half-reactions, overall reaction, cell notation, emf calculation, 'flat' cell at equilibrium
Standard electrode potentials; standard hydrogen electrode as reference
Electrolytic cells: ion movement, electron flow, half-reactions, overall reaction
Electrolytic applications: decomposition of CuCl2, electroplating, refining of copper, electrolysis of concentrated NaCl

sba: Formal practical (Physics): internal resistance of a battery; equivalent resistance of series/parallel resistors
Formal practical (Chemistry): verify the reactions in a galvanic cell and an electrolytic cell

sba_guidelines: Learners do TWO experiments (ONE Chemistry, ONE Physics) for SBA, chosen from this ATP
Term 1: choose ONE experiment, record in Term 1
Term 2 OR Term 3: choose ONE experiment, record the mark in Term 3
Suggested formal experiments not chosen for SBA become informal experiments
